terra.problem: The passage says an idol is nothing, but it does not say there is nothing behind it. That claim goes beyond the text.
The claim that no idol holds any real power goes beyond Paul's statement that an idol is nothing in the world.
The passage does not say Moses would be the first to point the baker to Jesus. It also does not identify Moses as Israel's leader, so that fact needs an outside reference.
Identifying Elijah as a prophet of Israel is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
Paul does not say that being accustomed to idols is why their conscience is weak. He says that since it is weak, it is defiled.
Paul does not say the person in this example is encouraged to eat because he is still accustomed to idols. He describes him as having a weak conscience.
Saying he is not going to joke comments on how he tells the passage. He can simply say the moment is heavy.
Paul says Christ died for the weak brother and that sinning against brothers in this way is sinning against Christ. He does not state the first as the reason for the second.
The explanation says Christ's death for the brother is what makes this sin so serious. Paul does not state that reason.
